summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would change the Paid Parental Leave scheme so government payments go only to parents without enough employer-provided leave.

From 1 July 2016, a parent's employer-paid parental leave would reduce or cancel their government payment, and from 1 April 2016 employers would no longer be required to pass on government-funded leave to long-term staff.
Parents with employer payments worth less than the full government rate would get a top-up, and those with equal or more employer pay would get nothing from the scheme.
changes: It ensures government parental leave payments are targeted to parents who lack sufficient employer-provided leave.
It removes the requirement for employers to hand over government-funded parental leave pay to eligible long-term employees.
It reintroduces a measure from a 2014 bill that is before the Senate.
summary.affected: Working parents who receive employer-provided parental leave payments, and businesses that employ eligible long-term workers.
